subject: Alignment on early-exit fee, auto-renew timing, and billing cutover
messages:
From: Eliot Shaw <eliot.shaw@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions — auto-renew / termination for convenience

Camila,

Thanks for the draft order form. Two quick asks from our procurement side before we move to signatures:

1) Auto-renew: Can we move to a 12-month auto-renew with a 90-day written notice to opt out? Our finance team aligns renewals with quarter boundaries and needs more lead time.

2) Termination for convenience: Acme has a policy that any early-exit fee be capped to the lesser of 25% of remaining committed fees OR the equivalent of three months' invoice. A full 100% of remaining is a non-starter.

If you can provide a redline that reflects those two items (or propose compromise language), we can review internally and get back with a PO timeline. We expect procurement approval by 11/18 if we can reach alignment this week.

Appreciate it —
Eliot

--
Eliot Shaw
Head of Procurement, Acme Analytics
eliot.shaw@acmeanalytics.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Eliot Shaw <eliot.shaw@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions — auto-renew / termination for convenience

Eliot —

Thanks for the clarity and the timeline. Two quick signals from our side:

- Auto-renew: Our standard is a 12-month renewal with a 30-day opt-out because we operate capacity commitments against those terms. That said, we can be flexible on notice windows for larger ARR.

- Termination for convenience: We support a commercial compromise to limit wind-down exposure, but we typically ask to recover the unamortized committed amount (remaining months) or a negotiated fee rather than a fixed percent cap.

I'm looping Ben (Sales Legal) and Mina (Contracts) to see if we can draft compromise language that aligns with your 11/18 procurement cadence.

Proposed next step: Ben to share a redline with two options — (A) 60-day notice + 50% of remaining commitment; (B) 90-day notice + 25% cap (to match their ask) — so Acme can choose. Would that work?

Camila
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T14:40:00-08:00
Subject: Redwood_MSA_v2_redlines.docx — redline: exit fee + renewal timing (internal)

Team,

Attached is my redline of the MSA and Order Form. High level: I created two concrete options for the termination-for-convenience language so the customer has a clear binary (option A or B) and we keep the rest of the commercial terms intact. Highlights in the doc: 

- Option A: 60-day written notice; termination fee equals 50% of the remaining committed fees (pro-rated monthly).
- Option B: 90-day written notice; termination fee capped at 25% of remaining committed fees OR three months' average monthly fees, whichever is lower.
- Auto-renew: Default remains 12 months; our standard opt-out window is 30 days, but I added an exception clause that allows larger customers to request 60/90 day notice in the Order Form if requested.

I also added a short billing-cutover paragraph: if termination occurs in the middle of a billing cycle, the fee is calculated to the end of that billing month to avoid proration disputes.

Mina — please sanity-check for procurement (PO / billing) implications and add the Order Form PDF after you validate round-trip with finance.

Ben
Legal Counsel, Sales Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Eliot Shaw <eliot.shaw@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@acmeanalytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-06T08:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions — auto-renew / termination for convenience

Eliot —

Ben attached two clean options in the redline (see attached 'Redwood_MSA_v2_redlines.docx') so you can pick whichever matches Acme's risk tolerance. Short summary:

- Option A: 60-day notice + 50% remaining commitment (less operationally disruptive for us).
- Option B: 90-day notice + 25% cap / or three months' fees (whichever is lower) — mirrors your request more closely.

Ben also included a billing-cutover clause to ensure the fee calculation matches invoice periods. If you want, we can mark Option B as the Order Form preference for enterprise customers and keep Option A as our default. That gives you procurement the 90-day timing you asked for while preserving our commercial fallback.

If this is acceptable, can you confirm by EOD 11/09 so we can lock the PO and route to DocuSign? Our finance team needs a PO reference to complete internal provisioning.

Thanks —
Camila

From: Eliot Shaw <eliot.shaw@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-11-06T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions — auto-renew / termination for convenience

Camila/Ben —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. We prefer Option B (90-day notice + 25% cap / three months floor). A couple of clarifying asks before we sign: 

1) Can you add a line that the termination-for-convenience calculation excludes any usage-based overages billed after the termination effective date? Finance needs the math to be predictable.
2) Confirm that the 90-day notice can be triggered by either party (not just Acme). We typically ask for symmetric rights.

If you can address 1–2 and issue the final Order Form with Option B marked, we will aim to get procurement approval and a PO to you on 11/18.

Eliot

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Eliot Shaw <eliot.shaw@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-09T15:43:00-08:00
Subject: Finalized - Option B accepted, next steps and DocuSign link

Eliot —

Great — glad to see Option B works. Per your asks, we've made two clarifications in the final Order Form: 

- Usage overages billed after the termination effective date are excluded from the termination-for-convenience calculation (they will be invoiced and settled on the normal payment terms).
- The 90-day notice right is symmetric — either party may provide written notice to terminate for convenience.

Attached: final "OrderForm_Acme_202611.pdf" with Option B clearly marked and the billing-cutover language inserted. DocuSign link for signature: https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/ACME-REDWOOD-EXE-202611 (also added to HubSpot).

Next steps on our side: Mina will create the provisioning ticket once we have the PO / fully executed Order Form. Please include your PO reference in the DocuSign comments so finance can reconcile.

If anything else comes up, ping me directly. Congrats — excited to get Acme onboarded.

Best,
Camila
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai
